content.prompt: Sketch the following on a number line.

answer.short: Closed segments from $-2$ to $2$ and from $3$ to $4$.
answer.worked: The union contains $-2\le x\le2$ or $3\le x\le4$. Draw both segments with filled circles at all four endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher page 585, Exercise 1I Essential Problems, answer 30, first number-line row left
spec.description: Two closed segments above a separate arrowed baseline, integer labels from -3 to 5.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer editions only; no student-side diagram or scaffold.
spec.shadingDecision: No region shading. Black filled endpoint markers encode inclusion.

answer.short: Segments from $1$ inclusive to $2$ exclusive and from $3$ inclusive to $4$ exclusive.
answer.worked: The union contains $1\le x<2$ or $3\le x<4$. Draw filled circles at $1$ and $3$, and open circles at $2$ and $4$.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher page 585, Exercise 1I Essential Problems, answer 31, first number-line row right
spec.description: Two segments above a separate baseline; filled left endpoints, open right endpoints; integer ticks 0 to 5.
spec.shadingDecision: No region shading. Filled markers encode inclusion; white marker interiors preserve excluded endpoints.

answer.short: Segments from $0$ inclusive to $1$ exclusive and from $2$ exclusive to $3$ inclusive.
answer.worked: The union contains $0\le x<1$ or $2<x\le3$. Draw filled circles at $0$ and $3$, and open circles at $1$ and $2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher page 585, Exercise 1I Essential Problems, answer 32, second number-line row left
spec.description: Segments [0,1) and (2,3] above a separate baseline, integer ticks -1 to 4.
spec.mathematics: Filled endpoints 0 and 3; open endpoints 1 and 2.
spec.shadingDecision: No region shading. Endpoint fills and white interiors encode inclusion and exclusion.

answer.short: Segments from $-2$ exclusive to $1$ inclusive and from $2$ exclusive to $4$ exclusive.
answer.worked: The union contains $-2<x\le1$ or $2<x<4$. Draw a filled circle at $1$ and open circles at $-2$, $2$ and $4$.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher page 585, Exercise 1I Essential Problems, answer 33, second number-line row right
spec.description: Two segments above a separate baseline, integer ticks -3 to 5.
spec.shadingDecision: No region shading. Filled and open endpoint markers carry mathematical meaning.

answer.short: A leftward ray including $-1$ and a rightward ray excluding $1$.
answer.worked: The union contains $x\le-1$ or $x>1$. Draw a filled circle at $-1$ with a leftward ray, and an open circle at $1$ with a rightward ray.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher page 585, Exercise 1I Essential Problems, answer 34, third number-line row left
spec.description: Outward rays above a separate baseline with integer ticks -3 to 3.
spec.shadingDecision: No region shading. Endpoint fill distinguishes inclusion; arrows indicate unbounded extent.

answer.short: The whole real number line except $1$, with an open circle at $1$.
answer.worked: The union contains $x<1$ or $x>1$. Neither interval includes $1$, so draw rays in both directions with an open circle at $1$.

spec.sourceRegion: Teacher page 585, Exercise 1I Essential Problems, answer 35, third number-line row right
spec.description: Two rays meeting at one excluded point above a separate baseline, integer ticks -1 to 3.
spec.mathematics: All real numbers except 1; one open marker at 1 and outward arrows.
spec.shadingDecision: No region shading. White open-point mask prevents the ray stroke from filling the excluded point.
